title: Amiakhum & Velakhum: Navigating Bangladesh's Deepest Canyon Trails
author: Tamim Hasan
summary: Standing atop the boulder-strewn gorge of Amiakhum in Thanchi, the roaring water echoing through the misty hills of Bandarban reminds you why we travel in groups.
content:
Standing atop the boulder-strewn gorge of Amiakhum in Thanchi, the roaring water echoing through the misty hills of Bandarban reminds you why we travel in groups. Our 14-member squad from Travelers of Bangladesh embarked from Ruma Bazar, navigating bamboo rafts across Remakri and trekking through steep rocky ledges with local Marma guides.

Traveling with a cooperative group transforms tough mountain trails into lifelong memories. We shared dry rations, helped each other scale slippery cliff passes, and set up our riverside camp under a canopy of stars. When heavy afternoon mist rolled in over Nafakhum falls, having experienced trail leaders ensured everyone crossed safely without a single twisted ankle.

For anyone planning this expedition: ensure high-grip trekking boots, waterproof dry-bags for all electronics, and always respect local indigenous customs. Never leave plastic waste on the trails. Our travel group organizes monthly ethical expeditions across Bandarban, Rangamati, and remote haors—come trek with us!

title: Floating in Silence: A Starlit Night in Tanguar Haor on a Wooden Bajra
author: Farzana Yasmin
summary: As the sun dipped behind the Meghalaya hills across the border, the vast waters of Tanguar Haor turned into a sheet of liquid amber.
content:
As the sun dipped behind the Meghalaya hills across the border, the vast waters of Tanguar Haor turned into a sheet of liquid amber. Our travel collective boarded a traditional wooden bajra in Tahirpur, deliberately turning off the diesel generator to experience the haor in its pure, tranquil silence.

Our group focuses on eco-conscious slow travel. We source our freshwater fish and duck curry directly from local community boatmen, strictly avoid all single-use plastics, and hold evening acoustic Baul folk singing sessions on the open roof deck.

Tanguar Haor is an ecological sanctuary. If you want to travel with our small circle of writers, photographers, and nature lovers, connect with Chhayanaut Wanderers for our upcoming winter migratory bird-watching journey.

title: Crossing the Keokradong Ridge to Boga Lake: Lessons in Teamwork
author: Sabbir Hossain
summary: The ascent to Boga Lake during changing weather taught our 10-person trek team the true value of pacing and camaraderie.
content:
The ascent to Boga Lake during changing weather taught our 10-person trek team the true value of pacing and camaraderie. Starting early from Koikhongjhiri, the steep clay trails challenged our endurance, but our sweepers and navigators kept morale soaring with upbeat banter and regular hydration checks.

Reaching the deep, mysterious waters of Boga Lake just as dusk fell felt like stepping into an ancient folklore. We lodged in wooden Bawm homestays, sharing steaming plates of mountain chicken and hill-grown red rice.

Bengal Trekkers Guild welcomes newcomers and seasoned hikers alike. We provide pre-trek fitness guidance and comprehensive first-aid coverage on every expedition. Check our page to learn more about our upcoming Sylhet cave exploration!
